s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion and associated skin changes
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation of the affected skin
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral, affecting the right thigh and buttock
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings included normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Alcian blue staining was negative
Patient was born to healthy parents and did not have any prior medical disease

differentials: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn
per_call: Subcutaneous fat necrosis of the newborn

shortlist.label: Stiff skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening and histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and adipocyte entrapment

shortlist.label: Segmental stiff skin syndrome (SSS)
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the segmental distribution of skin hardening and associated skin changes

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea)
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the linear distribution of skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of skin thickening and T2 signal abnormality on MRI, although eosinophilia is not mentioned

shortlist.label: Morphea profunda
shortlist.why_kept: A subtype of morphea that could explain the deep tissue involvement and skin changes

raw.rationale: The patient's unilateral skin hardening, lack of inflammation, and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis are consistent with Segmental stiff skin syndrome (SSS). The condition's progressive nature and the patient's age also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stiff skin syndrome
rejected.why: Stiff skin syndrome typically presents with more widespread skin involvement and often has a congenital or early infancy onset.

rejected.label: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea)
rejected.why: Linear Scleroderma (Morphea) often presents with distinct linear or band-like lesions and may have a more rapid progression than seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic fasciitis is characterized by rapid onset, widespread involvement, and often elevated eosinophil counts, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Morphea profunda
rejected.why: Morphea profunda is a subtype of morphea that affects deeper tissue, but the patient's presentation and histopathological findings do not align closely with this condition.
